L21: ## Key Terms
L22: 
L23: anatomical sphincter
L24:     smooth or skeletal muscle surrounding the lumen of a vessel or hollow organ that can restrict flow when contracted
L25: 
L26: angiotensin I
L27:     protein produced by the enzymatic action of renin on angiotensinogen; inactive precursor of angiotensin II
L28: 
L29: angiotensin II
L30:     protein produced by the enzymatic action of ACE on inactive angiotensin I; actively causes vasoconstriction and stimulates aldosterone release by the adrenal cortex
L31: angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE)
L32:     enzyme produced by the lungs that catalyzes the reaction of inactive angiotensin I into active angiotensin II
L33: 
L34: angiotensinogen
L35:     inactive protein in the circulation produced by the liver; precursor of angiotensin I; must be modified by the enzymes renin and ACE to be activated
L36: 
L37: anuria
L38:     absence of urine produced; production of 50 mL or less per day
L39: aquaporin
L40:     protein-forming water channels through the lipid bilayer of the cell; allows water to cross; activation in the collecting ducts is under the control of ADH
L41: 
L42: Bowman’s capsule
L43:     cup-shaped sack lined by a simple squamous epithelium (parietal surface) and specialized cells called podocytes (visceral surface) that participate in the filtration process; receives the filtrate which then passes on to the PCTs
L44: brush border
L45:     formed by microvilli on the surface of certain cuboidal cells; in the kidney it is found in the PCT; increases surface area for absorption in the kidney
L46: 
L47: calyces
L48:     cup-like structures receiving urine from the collecting ducts where it passes on to the renal pelvis and ureter
L49: 
L50: cortical nephrons
L51:     nephrons with loops of Henle that do not extend into the renal medulla
L52: countercurrent multiplier system
L53:     involves the descending and ascending loops of Henle directing forming urine in opposing directions to create a concentration gradient when combined with variable permeability and sodium pumping
L54: 
L55: detrusor muscle
L56:     smooth muscle in the bladder wall; fibers run in all directions to reduce the size of the organ when emptying it of urine
L57: distal convoluted tubules
L58:     portions of the nephron distal to the loop of Henle that receive hyposmotic filtrate from the loop of Henle and empty into collecting ducts
L59: 
L60: diuretic
L61:     compound that increases urine output, leading to decreased water conservation
L62: 
L63: efferent arteriole
L64:     arteriole carrying blood from the glomerulus to the capillary beds around the convoluted tubules and loop of Henle; portion of the portal system
L65: endothelins
L66:     group of vasoconstrictive, 21-amino acid peptides; produced by endothelial cells of the renal blood vessels, mesangial cells, and cells of the DCT
L67: 
L68: external urinary sphincter
L69:     skeletal muscle; must be relaxed consciously to void urine
L70: 
L71: fenestrations
L72:     small windows through a cell, allowing rapid filtration based on size; formed in such a way as to allow substances to cross through a cell without mixing with cell contents
L73: filtration slits
L74:     formed by pedicels of podocytes; substances filter between the pedicels based on size
L75: 
L76: forming urine
L77:     filtrate undergoing modifications through secretion and reabsorption before true urine is produced
L78: 
L79: glomerular filtration rate (GFR)
L80:     rate of renal filtration
L81: 
L82: glomerulus
L83:     tuft of capillaries surrounded by Bowman’s capsule; filters the blood based on size
L84: glycosuria
L85:     presence of glucose in the urine; caused by high blood glucose levels that exceed the ability of the kidneys to reabsorb the glucose; usually the result of untreated or poorly controlled diabetes mellitus
L86: 
L87: incontinence
L88:     loss of ability to control micturition
L89: 
L90: intercalated cell
L91:     specialized cell of the collecting ducts that secrete or absorb acid or bicarbonate; important in acid–base balance
L92: internal urinary sphincter
L93:     smooth muscle at the juncture of the bladder and urethra; relaxes as the bladder fills to allow urine into the urethra
L94: 
L95: inulin
L96:     plant polysaccharide injected to determine GFR; is neither secreted nor absorbed by the kidney, so its appearance in the urine is directly proportional to its filtration rate
L97: juxtaglomerular apparatus (JGA)
L98:     located at the juncture of the DCT and the afferent and efferent arterioles of the glomerulus; plays a role in the regulation of renal blood flow and GFR
L99: 
L100: juxtaglomerular cell
L101:     modified smooth muscle cells of the afferent arteriole; secretes renin in response to a drop in blood pressure
L102: 
L103: juxtamedullary nephrons
L104:     nephrons adjacent to the border of the cortex and medulla with loops of Henle that extend into the renal medulla
L105: leaky tight junctions
L106:     tight junctions in which the sealing strands of proteins between the membranes of adjacent cells are fewer in number and incomplete; allows limited intercellular movement of solvent and solutes
L107: 
L108: leukocyte esterase
L109:     enzyme produced by leukocytes that can be detected in the urine and that serves as an indirect indicator of urinary tract infection
L110: loop of Henle
L111:     descending and ascending portions between the proximal and distal convoluted tubules; those of cortical nephrons do not extend into the medulla, whereas those of juxtamedullary nephrons do extend into the medulla
L112: 
L113: macula densa
L114:     cells found in the part of the DCT forming the JGA; sense Na^{+} concentration in the forming urine
L115: 
L116: medulla
L117:     inner region of kidney containing the renal pyramids
L118: mesangial
L119:     contractile cells found in the glomerulus; can contract or relax to regulate filtration rate
L120: 
L121: micturition
L122:     also called urination or voiding
L123: 
L124: myogenic mechanism
L125:     mechanism by which smooth muscle responds to stretch by contracting; an increase in blood pressure causes vasoconstriction and a decrease in blood pressure causes vasodilation so that blood flow downstream remains steady
L126: nephrons
L127:     functional units of the kidney that carry out all filtration and modification to produce urine; consist of renal corpuscles, proximal and distal convoluted tubules, and descending and ascending loops of Henle; drain into collecting ducts
L128: 
L129: net filtration pressure (NFP)
L130:     pressure of fluid across the glomerulus; calculated by taking the hydrostatic pressure of the capillary and subtracting the colloid osmotic pressure of the blood and the hydrostatic pressure of Bowman’s capsule
L131: oliguria
L132:     below normal urine production of 400–500 mL/day
L133: 
L134: osteomalacia
L135:     softening of bones due to a lack of mineralization with calcium and phosphate; most often due to lack of vitamin D; in children, osteomalacia is termed rickets; not to be confused with osteoporosis
L136: 
L137: pedicels
L138:     finger-like projections of podocytes surrounding glomerular capillaries; interdigitate to form a filtration membrane
L139: peritubular capillaries
L140:     second capillary bed of the renal portal system; surround the proximal and distal convoluted tubules; associated with the vasa recta
L141: 
L142: physiological sphincter
L143:     sphincter consisting of circular smooth muscle indistinguishable from adjacent muscle but possessing differential innervations, permitting its function as a sphincter; structurally weak
L144: podocytes
L145:     cells forming finger-like processes; form the visceral layer of Bowman’s capsule; pedicels of the podocytes interdigitate to form a filtration membrane
L146: 
L147: polyuria
L148:     urine production in excess of 2.5 L/day; may be caused by diabetes insipidus, diabetes mellitus, or excessive use of diuretics
L149: principal cell
L150:     found in collecting ducts and possess channels for the recovery or loss of sodium and potassium; under the control of aldosterone; also have aquaporin channels under ADH control to regulate recovery of water
L151: 
L152: proximal convoluted tubules (PCTs)
L153:     tortuous tubules receiving filtrate from Bowman’s capsule; most active part of the nephron in reabsorption and secretion
L154: renal columns
L155:     extensions of the renal cortex into the renal medulla; separates the renal pyramids; contains blood vessels and connective tissues
L156: 
L157: renal corpuscle
L158:     consists of the glomerulus and Bowman’s capsule
L159: 
L160: renal cortex
L161:     outer part of kidney containing all of the nephrons; some nephrons have loops of Henle extending into the medulla
L162: 
L163: renal fat pad
L164:     adipose tissue between the renal fascia and the renal capsule that provides protective cushioning to the kidney
L165: renal hilum
L166:     recessed medial area of the kidney through which the renal artery, renal vein, ureters, lymphatics, and nerves pass
L167: 
L168: renal papillae
L169:     medullary area of the renal pyramids where collecting ducts empty urine into the minor calyces
L170: 
L171: renal pyramids
L172:     six to eight cone-shaped tissues in the medulla of the kidney containing collecting ducts and the loops of Henle of juxtamedullary nephrons
L173: renin
L174:     enzyme produced by juxtaglomerular cells in response to decreased blood pressure or sympathetic nervous activity; catalyzes the conversion of angiotensinogen into angiotensin I
L175: 
L176: retroperitoneal
L177:     behind the peritoneum; in the case of the kidney and ureters, between the parietal peritoneum and the abdominal wall
L178: sacral micturition center
L179:     group of neurons in the sacral region of the spinal cord that controls urination; acts reflexively unless its action is modified by higher brain centers to allow voluntary urination
L180: 
L181: specific gravity
L182:     weight of a liquid compared to pure water, which has a specific gravity of 1.0; any solute added to water will increase its specific gravity
L183: systemic edema
L184:     increased fluid retention in the interstitial spaces and cells of the body; can be seen as swelling over large areas of the body, particularly the lower extremities
L185: 
L186: trigone
L187:     area at the base of the bladder marked by the two ureters in the posterior–lateral aspect and the urethral orifice in the anterior aspect oriented like points on a triangle
L188: tubuloglomerular feedback
L189:     feedback mechanism involving the JGA; macula densa cells monitor Na^{+} concentration in the terminal portion of the ascending loop of Henle and act to cause vasoconstriction or vasodilation of afferent and efferent arterioles to alter GFR
L190: 
L191: urethra
L192:     transports urine from the bladder to the outside environment
L193: 
L194: urinalysis
L195:     analysis of urine to diagnose disease
L196: 
L197: urochrome
L198:     heme-derived pigment that imparts the typical yellow color of urine
L199: vasa recta
L200:     branches of the efferent arterioles that parallel the course of the loops of Henle and are continuous with the peritubular capillaries; with the glomerulus, form a portal system
